name: Park UI (on Ark UI + Panda CSS + Radix Colors)
vendor: Christian Schroeter / Brains & Pixels design; now under the Chakra UI organisation (Chakra Systems Inc.). Ark UI is by Chakra Systems Inc.
licence: MIT (github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui, Copyright 2025 cschroeter, studied commit 102769c 2026-02-21; Ark UI github.com/chakra-ui/ark MIT, @ark-ui/react 5.39.3; Radix Colors MIT; Panda CSS MIT)
bestFor: teams that want to OWN the component source (copy-paste via CLI) and edit recipes directly
products where one accent colour plus one tuned gray is the whole brand (SaaS dashboards, tools, docs)
multi-framework codebases (React, Solid, Vue) sharing one visual spec via Ark UI behaviour
projects that care about perceptually-consistent light and dark palettes (Radix 12-step scales)
avoidFor: editorial or expressive brand sites (no type voice, 4px radii, flat, quiet)
teams without a Panda CSS build step (static extraction, codegen) or who want a prebuilt npm component package
very dense data tables (control heights start at 24px and default to 40px)

families: sans: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif, Apple Color Emoji, Segoe UI Emoji, Segoe UI Symbol, Noto Color Emoji (Panda preset; Park UI sets no font)
serif: ui-serif, Georgia, Cambria, Times New Roman, Times, serif
mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, Liberation Mono, Courier New, monospace
docs site only: Outfit (body), Roboto Mono (code)
typography.notes: textStyles pair size, line-height and (4xl+) -0.02em tracking, same ladder as Chakra v3 except xs has 18px leading (Chakra 16px) and tracking is -0.02em (Chakra -0.025em). Font weights come from the Panda preset (thin 100 ... black 900). Buttons, tabs, headings are semibold 600; labels, badges, switch labels medium 500. fontSizes include 2xs 8px (Panda) but no Park UI style uses it. Park UI ships NO typeface: type voice is entirely the host project's choice. Tabular numerals are set on Badge.

neutrals.note: Radix Colors, 12 steps per mode PLUS 12 alpha steps (a1-a12) per mode, 31 scales (6 grays + 25 chromatic). Step semantics (Radix): 1 app background, 2 subtle background, 3 component bg, 4 component hover, 5 component pressed/selected, 6 subtle border (non-interactive), 7 interactive border, 8 stronger border/focus ring, 9 solid (highest chroma), 10 solid hover, 11 low-contrast text, 12 high-contrast text.

accents.note: 25 chromatic + neutral selectable as accent: tomato, red, ruby, crimson, pink, plum, purple, violet, iris, indigo, blue, cyan, teal, jade, green, grass, bronze, gold, brown, orange, amber, yellow, lime, mint, sky. Step 9 is the brand colour in both modes.

per-palette variant contract (every acce.solid: bg = step 9, bg.hover = step 10, fg = white (neutral: bg black/white inverted, hover gray.12)
per-palette variant contract (every acce.subtle: bg = alpha a3, bg.hover = a4, bg.active = a5, fg = a11
per-palette variant contract (every acce.surface: bg = a2, bg.active = a3, border = a6, border.hover = a7, fg = a11
per-palette variant contract (every acce.outline: border = a7, bg.hover = a2, bg.active = a3, fg = a11
per-palette variant contract (every acce.plain: bg.hover = a3, bg.active = a4, fg = a11 (neutral gray fg = gray.12)

semantic.bright-solid exception: amber, yellow, lime, mint and sky use fg = gray.12 on solid in light mode and gray.1 in dark mode (dark text on bright fills); all other chromatic solids use white

color.darkMode: Each Radix scale is hand-authored for both modes (not inverted by formula), so step N means the same role in light and dark. The theme stores {_light, _dark} on every step and switches by the `.dark` class condition (Panda `_dark`, plus a `light` condition ':root &, .light &'). Variant tokens use ALPHA steps (a3, a6, a11) over whatever surface they sit on, which keeps tints correct on any canvas. Shadows have a dark twin with black.a8 drop plus a 1px inset gray.a8 edge.
color.contrastNotes: Radix guarantees steps 11 and 12 reach APCA Lc 60 and Lc 90 on a step 2 background of the same scale (Radix docs, checked). Measured WCAG 2 (this study): white on blue.9 = 3.26:1, white on red.9 = 3.91:1, white on green.9 = 3.16:1 (solid steps are mid-lightness and fail 4.5:1 for 14px labels; they pass only as large text or with APCA); amber.9 with gray.12 = 10.32:1; sky.9 with gray.12 = 10.99:1; blue.11 on blue.2 = 4.53:1; blue.12 on blue.2 = 12.00:1; red.11 on red.2 = 4.94:1; neutral fg.muted gray.11 on canvas = 5.77:1; fg.subtle gray.10 on canvas = 3.70:1 (placeholder, below 4.5:1); dark: gray.11 on gray.1 = 9.11:1, gray.10 on gray.1 = 4.46:1. Subtle/surface text uses alpha a11, so its effective contrast depends on the surface behind it (the numbers above use opaque step 11 as the proxy).

radius.rule: Three semantic layers: l1 = radii.xs (2px), l2 = radii.sm (4px), l3 = radii.md (6px) in the preset. l1 sits inside l2 which sits inside l3 (docs: 'makes it easy to nest border radii'; l1 smallest, used inside other elements; l2 medium, wraps l1; l3 largest, wraps l2). Controls (Button, Input, Badge) use l2; panels use l3; Switch uses full. The CLI prompt and website offer a border-radius scale (none, xs, sm default, md, lg, xl, 2xl), but in the studied CLI version (init.ts / prompt.ts) the value returned to the Panda config is fixed to xs/sm/md regardless of the answer, so in practice re-pointing the three tokens is a manual edit. Changing the character of the system = editing three token references.

shadows: xs: 0 1px 2px gray.a6, 0 0 1px gray.a7 (dark: 0 1px 1px black.a8, 0 0 1px inset gray.a8)
depth.borders: 1px everywhere. Surface variants use a real 1px border at alpha a6 (hover a7); outline uses a7; default card/field/table border = gray.4. Flushed input uses a 1px bottom border.
depth.blur: No blur tokens in the preset. Dialog and drawer backdrops are flat scrims.

motion.notes: Park UI overrides Panda's duration tokens: fastest 50, faster 100, fast 150, normal 200, slow 250, slower 300, slowest 400ms (Panda default has slow 300, slower 400, slowest 500). Open/closed pairs: menu, tooltip, popover = fast (150) in / faster (100) out; select = slow (250) in / fastest (50) out; dialog = normal (200) in / fast (150) out (backdrop slowest 400 in / normal out); accordion = normal both. Switch thumb moves in 0.12s ease. Keyframes: expand/collapse height and width, fade, slide, scale. Disabled: opacity 0.67 plus grayscale(100%) (layerStyle) with cursor not-allowed. No reduced-motion token. Transition shorthand: transition 'colors' with explicit property list (background-color, border-color, color, box-shadow).

modes: size prop on every component (2xs..2xl where applicable)
two component classes: primary (Button, Input, Select, Tabs triggers) and secondary (Badge, Checkbox, Switch, Radio)

list: (recipe files also cover Angle Slider, Listbox, Password Input, QR Code, Signature Pad, Steps, Timer, Toggle, Tour, Tree View)
components.stateMatrixCompleteness: Five shared variants everywhere (solid, subtle, surface, outline, plain), with the usage guidance in the docs (solid = primary CTA; subtle = badges, tags, selected; surface = cards, menu items, selectable lists; outline = secondary, filters, cancel; plain = text buttons, links, tabs, ghost actions). Sizes 2xs-2xl; primary components share heights per size token (md Button = md Input = 40px). States: hover (variant-specific token), active (_active / _on for toggled state), focus-visible (outside ring 2px offset 2px, or inside ring 1px for inputs/tab panels), disabled (layerStyle: opacity .67 + grayscale), invalid (error colour on border and ring), checked/indeterminate. Colour axis is colorPalette (any of 31 palettes) so state x variant x palette is complete by construction. Missing: no loading state in the Button recipe (a Spinner is composed manually), no density/mode switch, reduced-motion not addressed.

tokenArchitecture: Layers: (1) Panda base presets (@pandacss/preset-base utilities + preset-panda scales for fonts, fontSizes, spacing, sizes, radii, durations, easings, shadows). (2) Park UI preset: tokens (black/white alpha colours, durations, zIndex), semanticTokens colors = 31 Radix scales each with steps 1-12, a1-a12 and variant tokens (solid, subtle, surface, outline, plain x bg/border/fg x default/hover/active), gray alias = chosen neutral, aliases fg.default/muted/subtle, canvas, border, error; semantic shadows xs-2xl, radii l1/l2/l3; textStyles; layerStyles (disabled); animationStyles; keyframes; conditions (light, invalid, hover = :not(:disabled):hover, active, checked, on, pinned); globalCss. (3) recipes/slotRecipes bound to Ark UI anatomy (e.g. tabsAnatomy.keys(), switchAnatomy.extendWith('indicator')), written once and copied into the app as source. (4) Ark UI: headless, state-machine (Zag.js) components with data-scope / data-part / data-state attributes that the recipes target via conditions (_open, _closed, _checked, _selected, _horizontal). Consumers choose framework (react or solid in the CLI prompt), accentColor and grayColor at `init` (borderRadius is prompted but not applied in the studied CLI); there is no runtime theme switching. Names: colorPalette.{variant}.{bg|border|fg}.{hover|active}; scale steps numeric 1-12 and a1-a12.
distinctiveness: The product-level idea is one accent + one matched gray from Radix Colors, expressed as a fixed five-variant vocabulary on every component, with copy-paste owned recipes. Visually it is quiet: 4px radius, hairline borders, alpha-tinted fills, Radix 12-step colour. Recognisable by alpha-over-surface tints (subtle/surface), mauve/sage/sand/slate tinted grays, and primary controls that share one height ladder (24/32/36/40/44/48/64).
weaknesses: No typeface or type voice shipped: identity must be added by the project
Solid step 9 fills measure 3.16-3.91:1 against white text (blue, green, red), so default solid buttons miss WCAG AA for small labels (except bright palettes that switch to dark text)
fg.subtle (gray.10) is 3.70:1 on canvas and is also used for placeholder
Disabled uses opacity 0.67 + grayscale, a heavy effect applied uniformly
No reduced-motion handling in the preset and no pressed state for solid buttons beyond hover colour
Requires Panda CSS static extraction and codegen; recipes are copied, so upgrades mean manual merges
Alpha-based tints make contrast depend on the surface behind them (hard to guarantee statically)
takeaways: Use a 12-step role scale (1 canvas, 2 subtle bg, 3-5 component bg rest/hover/pressed, 6-8 borders subtle/interactive/strong+focus, 9-10 solid/hover, 11-12 text low/high) for every hue and gray, hand-tuned per mode, so step numbers carry meaning.

Choose ONE accent and ONE gray whose hue matches the accent (pairings: mauve with pink/purple, slate with blue/indigo, sage with green/teal, olive with lime, sand with amber/orange); neutral is the safe default.
Fix a five-variant vocabulary shared by all components (solid, subtle, surface, outline, plain) and document each variant's use, so mixed components always match.
Define variant tokens once per palette as {variant}.{bg|border|fg}.{hover|active}, using ALPHA steps for tints so they sit correctly on any surface.
Align heights across component families: primary controls share one ladder (24/32/36/40/44/48/64) and secondary controls share another, so a Button and Input of the same size are the same height.
Provide three nested radius layers (l1 inside l2 inside l3) so the global character is a three-token edit.
Handle bright palettes explicitly: amber, yellow, lime, mint, sky take dark foreground on solid fills in both modes.
Pair open/close durations asymmetrically (150 in / 100 out; select 250 in / 50 out) and keep the duration tokens small (50-400).
Prefer copy-paste ownership of recipes with a tiny preset: components are data (recipes) the project edits, not a package API.
